wrong_text: Duplex board (folding boxboard) — a two-ply board with a bleached white top layer for printing and a grey recycled-fibre back.
problem: Duplex board and folding boxboard are distinct materials and must not be equated in parentheses. Duplex board (grey-back / GD grade) has one white printable side and a grey recycled-fibre back — it is a lower-cost, single-sided print board. Folding boxboard (FBB / GC grade) is white on both sides, with bleached chemical-pulp outer plies over a mechanical-pulp middle layer, and is a premium grade used for pharmaceutical, cosmetic and food-contact cartons. The Eduqas GCSE D&T specification and revision materials list them as separate board types. Labelling them as the same in a GCSE lesson will produce wrong exam answers on any question that asks students to name or distinguish board grades.
correction: Duplex board — a board with a bleached white top layer for printing and a grey recycled-fibre back. Used for food packaging, cereal boxes and cosmetics cartons where a high-quality printed surface is required at moderate cost.

wrong_text: Used in food packaging (butter wrappers, ready-meal trays, coffee pouches) and drinks cartons.
problem: Foil-lined board is a flat laminated cartonboard used for folded/glued cartons, wrappers and pouches — it cannot be formed into a tray. Ready-meal trays are rigid containers made from solid-aluminium foil (e.g. smoothwall foil trays) or moulded paperboard, not foil-lined board. Including 'ready-meal trays' as an application conflates two fundamentally different packaging formats and mis-teaches what foil-lined board actually is.
correction: Used in food packaging (butter wrappers, confectionery cartons, coffee pouches) and drinks cartons.
